en.title: Seasonal festivals
en.summary: Festivals tied to the seasons, such as Bonfire Night, Halloween and May Day.

paragraphs: Many festivals mark the changing seasons. This lesson introduces the main ones in Britain and North America and the grammar of plans with going to.

Autumn is full of festivals. On 31 October children dress up and go from door to door at Halloween, which is especially popular in the United States. On 5 November British people watch fireworks and bonfires on Bonfire Night, which remembers a failed plot of 1605 to blow up Parliament. Two children discuss their plans.

lines.speaker: Max
lines.text: Are you going to the fireworks on the fifth of November?

lines.speaker: Ivy
lines.text: Yes. We're going to watch the bonfire and eat toffee apples.

lines.speaker: Max
lines.text: I'm dressing up for Halloween first.

lines.speaker: Max
lines.text: A ghost! My mum is going to make the costume.

lines.speaker: Ivy
lines.text: I'm going as a witch. We're going to collect sweets.

lines.speaker: Max
lines.text: Be careful on the street. It's going to be dark.

paragraphs: **1. Be going to expresses a plan.** Use am, is or are + going to + base verb for plans decided before the moment of speaking. See Introduction to Grammar: Future and other tenses.

blocks.html:
FormExample
statementWe are going to watch the bonfire.
questionAre you going to come?
negativeI'm not going to dress up.
predictionIt's going to be dark.

paragraphs: **2. Go as and dress up as say which character you are.** Dress up is a phrasal verb, and as links you with the character. See Introduction to Grammar: Prepositions and conjunctions.

blocks.html:
PhraseExample
go asI'm going as a ghost.
dress up asShe dressed up as a witch.
come asCome as your favourite character.
wearI'm going to wear a mask.

items: Bonfire Night (5 November) remembers a failed plot of 1605.
Halloween is on 31 October; trick or treat is the custom of asking for sweets.
May Day marks the start of summer in many villages, with a maypole and dancing.
A toffee apple is an apple covered in hard toffee.

paragraphs: Many British villages hold harvest festivals in autumn and fairs in spring and summer. In the United States, Halloween decorations, such as carved pumpkins, appear in shops weeks before the day.
